criteria.name: Analytical grounding
criteria.definition: Does the education section state a qualification or a course of structured study whose method is the one this role's structured problem solving competency describes, taking an unfamiliar problem apart and defending the answer to somebody who was not there? This criterion is named for the proxy it reads rather than for the competency it maps to, because an education section evidences grounding rather than the working an interview establishes.

criteria.name: Collaboration across teams
criteria.definition: Does an experience entry show a piece of a program carried forward with people who did not report to the candidate and held different priorities, rather than an outcome asserted?

criteria.name: Customer framing
criteria.definition: Is the summary written in the terms of the person on the other side of the work rather than in the internal terms of the team that did it?

criteria.name: Prioritization under constraint
criteria.definition: Does an experience entry name something the candidate said would not be done, and who they said it to, rather than listing everything that was delivered?

criteria.name: Operational rigor
criteria.definition: Does an experience entry name a record, a handover or a check the candidate built, of the kind that lets a process survive the absence of the person who designed it?

shortlist_guidance: The score ranks; it does not decide. Read the ranked list, then decide as a person who can be asked why, and record the reason beside the name. A resume that is missing one of the required fields is scored incomplete, with the missing field named, and is neither dropped from the list nor scored zero on the criteria it does answer: an incomplete record is a question to put to the candidate, not a verdict on them. Where two resumes sit within one point of each other, treat the ordering as arbitrary and say so rather than defending it. No criterion scores a quantified outcome, so a resume that states none is not disadvantaged; what is scored is what the candidate built, owned or decided.
